card.occupation: Part-time IT support technician, about 12 hours a week, split between a small accountancy firm in the town centre and a dental practice in Lindley. He looks after their laptops, printers, backups and Microsoft 365 accounts.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Huddersfield, then a BTEC National Diploma in IT at Huddersfield Technical College, followed by a part-time HNC in Computing. He later took CompTIA A+ and a Microsoft 365 administrator certificate through evening and online study in his thirties.
card.household: He lives with his partner Saima, 44, a teaching assistant at a local primary school, in a three-bed semi in Birkby. They had a nikah three years ago but haven't done a civil registration yet, which he's been meaning to sort out. His two children from his first marriage, Zain (17) and Aleena (14), live with their mum in Dewsbury. They stay with him every other weekend and come round for tea on Wednesdays.
card.cultural_background: Born in Huddersfield to parents from the Mirpur district of Pakistan. His dad came over in the late 1960s and worked nights in a textile mill, and his mum raised four children. He is British Pakistani and a practising Muslim, quietly so. He prays most of his daily prayers, goes to Friday prayers when work allows and fasts in Ramadan. He speaks Pahari-Pothwari and some Urdu with older relatives and English everywhere else. His mum died in 2020. His dad, now 79, lives ten minutes away with Imran's younger brother.
card.professional_persona: He spent nearly twenty years full-time in IT support, mostly at a college and then a logistics firm, and was a team leader for a while. Four years ago he cut his hours right down, partly after the divorce and his mum's death, and partly to be around for his dad's hospital appointments and for the kids. He is methodical and patient with non-technical staff. He documents everything, keeps a password-managed log for each client and labels cables. He'd rather fix a problem properly once than patch it twice. He doesn't like selling himself and gets most work by word of mouth.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong Yorkshire cricket follower. He played as a batsman in the Huddersfield league in his twenties and early thirties and now watches more than he plays, sometimes at Headingley with his son. He walks most days, often up to Castle Hill or along the canal, and tracks his steps carefully. Not a big football fan, though he keeps half an eye on Huddersfield Town results.
card.arts_persona: He listens to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and old qawwali in the car, along with some 90s British music from his college days, like Oasis, The Verve and Cornershop. He reads popular history, especially about the Partition and the Second World War, and gets through a book a month on his Kindle. He doesn't really go to galleries or the theatre.
card.travel_persona: He has visited Pakistan several times for family weddings and to see relatives, most recently in 2022. He did Umrah with his mum in 2019, which he holds very dear. Otherwise he prefers UK breaks: the Lake District, Whitby, the Yorkshire Dales. He plans trips well in advance, with a printed itinerary and booked parking. He doesn't enjoy flying much and gets anxious about connections.
card.culinary_persona: He cooks a reliable chicken karahi and his mum's tarka dal, which the kids ask for on Wednesday nights. Saima does more of the everyday cooking, but he does Saturday breakfast for the household: eggs, parathas, chai. He shops at the big halal butcher on the same day each week. He likes a fish and chip tea at the seaside and has a sweet tooth for jalebi and Yorkshire parkin alike.
hobbies_and_interests: Refurbishing old laptops and giving them to families at the local mosque and the kids' schools
Walking around Castle Hill and the Colne Valley
Keeping a tidy vegetable patch in the back garden (tomatoes, chillies, coriander)
Watching cricket highlights and documentaries with his son
skills: Clear step-by-step explanation for non-technical people
card.career_goals: He isn't chasing promotion. He'd like to gradually take on two or three more small-business clients so he can go up to about 20 hours once his dad's needs are clearer, while keeping Wednesdays and the kids' weekends free. He has thought about formally setting up as a sole trader with a proper website but keeps putting off the self-promotion side.
card.voice: Quiet, measured and polite, with a soft West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, 'tea' for the evening meal, the odd 'nowt' or 'reckon'. He thinks before answering, often starting with 'Er...' or 'Well, it's sort of...', and his answers are fairly short unless the topic is something he knows well, like computers, cricket or his kids, when he opens up more. He says 'sorry' readily, sometimes to correct himself ('sorry, I mean the other one'). He ends points with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. He doesn't fill silences himself. He waits, and might say 'Is that alright?' to check he's answered properly.
card.typing: Careful and correct. Proper capital letters, full stops, correct apostrophes, and usually complete sentences even in quick boxes. He rarely abbreviates beyond 'e.g.' or 'IT'. He sometimes reads back and corrects a typo before submitting. No emojis.
card.with_strangers: Courteous, a bit reserved and eager not to give the wrong answer. He comes across as kind and trustworthy rather than chatty. He'll ask a clarifying question rather than guess, and he warms up noticeably once he's put at ease or the conversation turns practical.
small_things: The dental practice's printer that 'jams if you look at it wrong'

Traffic on the A62 into Huddersfield

Missing his mum, and how much the Umrah trip with her means to him now
Worry about his dad's heart condition and who'll look after him long-term
Feeling a bit 'between' worlds: very Yorkshire, very Muslim, never quite fully either in some rooms
Wanting to make his relationship with Saima official legally and not having got round to it
Quiet anxiety about money since dropping his hours
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the view looks a little upward at him. He sits centred at a dining table, head and shoulders in frame. Soft daylight comes from a window off to the left, leaving the right side of his face a little shadowed. He's a South Asian man with light-brown skin, short black hair greying at the temples, and a neatly trimmed short beard flecked with grey. He wears thin black rectangular glasses and has a polite, slightly tentative half-smile. He's in a navy quarter-zip jumper over a white collared shirt. Behind him is a magnolia-painted wall with a framed black-and-gold Arabic calligraphy piece (Ayat al-Kursi) hung a little to the right. Below it is a low pine bookshelf holding a row of labelled ring binders, a few paperbacks, a small potted plant and a phone charging cable. The edge of a white radiator is visible at the bottom left.
